title: In Locarno, A/B groups explain 54% of the fitted count fall near 1981 at matched F10.7
abstract: We split Locarno weighted Wolf counts by Zurich class to test the fall near 1981 at matched emission. In November 1978 to June 1983, an additive spline model assigns 21.84 of the 40.21-unit radio-matched fall to classes A and B, which have no penumbrae. The count in other groups falls by 10.58% (conditional 95% interval -18.97% to -1.89%). Observer, seeing, activity-overlap and time-slope controls retain a negative additive radio effect. The main Mg II interval and a flat log-response overlap interval include zero. The A/B share changes from 54% to 23% when time slopes are added. A 1970 phase control is uncertain. The result opposes a loss confined to whole A/B groups under the main radio model. It does not exclude loss of small spots inside other groups, or distinguish solar change from shared counting changes. Code, aggregate estimates, input hashes and external-data retrieval instructions are included. External observations stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Fitted class changes near 1981 and in the 1970 phase control. Intervals are conditional 95% residual-block intervals. P includes groups with penumbrae; it also includes small spots within those groups.
